name: Morocco
headline: Moroccans can ask each doctor for a copy of their file, but no shared record exists yet; a July 2026 bill would create one.

access.summary: Law 131-13 says patients can obtain a copy of their medical file, and Law 09-08 makes access to personal data free. There is no national patient portal yet, and the law sets no fixed answer deadline.
detail: Article 2 of Law 131-13 (2015) on medical practice says the patient, a legal representative or heirs can obtain a copy of the medical file.

Article 7 of Law 09-08 gives a right to obtain one's data in intelligible form, at reasonable intervals, without delay and free of charge. A controller may ask the CNDP for extra time and may refuse requests that are clearly abusive.
The ministry said in April 2026 that the shared medical record had finished its technical phase and was ready for gradual rollout in 2026. A live patient portal was not verified.
Bill 52.26, adopted by the government on 22 July 2026, would give patients electronic access to their shared record. It is not yet law.

control.summary: Law 09-08 requires express consent or a legal basis to process sensitive data, but doctors need only declare health data processing to the CNDP. No national sharing system, opt-out or patient-visible access log exists yet.
detail: Article 21 of Law 09-08 ties processing of sensitive data to the person's express consent, a legal duty, or CNDP authorisation.
Article 22 relaxes this for health data used only for care by staff bound by professional secrecy: a declaration to the CNDP is enough, with no patient consent step.
Article 9 gives a right to object on legitimate grounds, except where processing meets a legal obligation.
Bill 52.26 would let patients hide some data from professionals, except in emergencies, and doctors would collect prior consent, according to press reports of the text. It is not yet law.

privacy.summary: Health data is sensitive data under Law 09-08, and processing it without express consent can bring three months to a year in prison and fines up to 300,000 dirhams. The law has no breach notification duty, and CNDP sanctions against health actors were not verified.
detail: Article 1 of Law 09-08 lists health and genetic data as sensitive. Article 24 sets extra security duties for anyone processing health data.
Article 57 punishes processing health data without express consent with 3 to 12 months in prison and fines of 50,000 to 300,000 dirhams.

Law 09-08 has no duty to notify breaches to the regulator or to patients. In April 2025 hackers leaked files on nearly 2 million people from the CNSS, the social security fund that runs private-sector health insurance; the CNDP said it would investigate complaints.
As a non-EU country, Morocco is outside the GDPR and the EHDS; an EU-funded CNDP gap study looked at aligning Law 09-08 with the GDPR.

commercial.summary: Law 09-08 gives a free right to refuse marketing use of personal data and bans automated direct marketing without consent. In 2024 the CNDP opened an inquiry into pharmacy software allegedly passing prescription data to drug makers; the outcome was not verified.
detail: Article 9 lets a person object, at no cost, to use of their data for marketing, including commercial prospecting.
Article 10 bans direct marketing by automated calls, fax or email without prior consent, with a narrow exception for existing customers.
Hespress reported in April 2024 that the CNDP was investigating a pharmacy software firm suspected of passing prescription and patient data, stored on a cloud in Belgium, to drug laboratories.
No specific rule on health data brokers or sale of de-identified health data was found. Bill 52.26 would ban use of the national health identifier outside the health system.

journey.summary: A shared medical record and an electronic care sheet are built but not yet in national use; a Kenitra care sheet pilot was planned for March 2026, and its launch was not verified. Hospitals, labs and private doctors still keep separate records.
detail: The 2022 framework law 06-22 names digitalisation as the fourth pillar of health reform. A 2024 agreement between the ministry, the CNSS and the Digital Development Agency aims to create a unified interface for the shared record and care sheet.
The CNSS electronic care sheet links doctors, pharmacists, labs and imaging centres by QR code. A Kenitra pilot was planned for March 2026, then national rollout from April to June.
The ministry said in April 2026 that a national platform pooling public and private data had finished development, with final rollout after consultation.
Bill 52.26 would require every public and private provider to connect within 24 months of its implementing decree.

clinical.summary: No national exchange lets a treating doctor see records held by other providers. The shared record was technically complete in April 2026 but its live use was not verified.
detail: Records stay with each hospital or practice. The ministry describes the shared record as a 2026 rollout, not a working service.
A territorial health group pilot in Tanger-Tetouan-Al Hoceima improved coordination between hospitals in that region, the ministry said.
Under Bill 52.26, a doctor could open a patient's record in a life-threatening emergency even where the patient has hidden data. It is not yet law.

research.summary: Law 28-13 requires free, informed, written consent for biomedical research and lets participants withdraw at any time. Observational studies on health data fall outside it and depend on Law 09-08, with CNDP authorisation and no general opt-out.
detail: Articles 4 to 6 of Law 28-13 require written, signed consent after oral and written information, and allow withdrawal at any time.
Article 2 says non-interventional and observational research is not covered by the law, apart from article 26, but must respect data protection law.
Under Law 09-08, reuse of data for a new purpose and processing of sensitive data need prior CNDP authorisation, granted on express consent or a legal basis. Article 57 penalties apply to misuse.
In 2022 the CNDP said it would develop joint work on health data with the Casablanca biomedical research ethics committee. No public register of data uses or general research opt-out was found.

ai.summary: Morocco has no AI law and no clinical AI rule. The 2013 device law covers software only as part of a device, and a March 2025 CNDP statement says Law 09-08 governs AI use of personal data, which puts it near the top of the no-rules band.
detail: Law 84-12 defines a medical device to include software needed for its operation and sets four risk classes. No rule on AI change control, validation or human oversight was found.
The CNDP said on 18 March 2025 that AI processing of personal data is governed by Law 09-08, and that day began hearings with institutions, parties and experts toward a CNDP deliberation on AI.
Article 7 of Law 09-08 gives people a right to know the logic behind automated processing of their data.
